# Part 1. Data Visualization

## Question 1
Use `datasets::mtcars` for Question 1.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

rmarkdown::paged_table(datasets::mtcars)
```

<br>

![](http://bcdanl.github.io/lec_figs/danl-310-hw2-q1.png)
<br>


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)

mtcars %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = disp, y = mpg, color = hp)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9, shape = 17) +  
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma",
    guide = guide_colorbar(direction = "vertical"),
    position = "right"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Displacement (cu. in.)",
    y = "Fuel efficiency (mpg)",
    color = "Horsepower",
  ) +
  theme_fivethirtyeight() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title.y = element_text(vjust =5),    
    axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -1),   
    plot.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8)
  )
```
```{r}
# Fuel efficiency decreases as displacement increases. Larger engines are less efficient. 
```

## Question 2

Use the following data.frame for Question 2.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
popgrowth_df <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/popgrowth.csv')
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

rmarkdown::paged_table(popgrowth_df)
```

<br>

![](http://bcdanl.github.io/lec_figs/danl-310-hw2-q2.png)
<br>


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)
library(scales)

popgrowth_df %>%
  mutate(
    state = fct_reorder(state, popgrowth),
    region = factor(region)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = state, y = popgrowth, fill = region)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +   # percentage axis
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "West" = "#FFF7AE",      
      "South" = "#D41159",
      "Northeast" = "#7E03A8",
      "Midwest" = "#000000"
    ),
    guide = guide_legend(
      ncol = 1,
      byrow = TRUE,
      title.position = "top"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Population Growth (2000–2010)",
    fill = "Region",
  ) +
  theme_fivethirtyeight() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )

```
```{r}
# West states have the highest increases where northeast states have a smaller increase. The horizontal layout easily compares all the different states. 
```

## Question 3
Use the following data.frame for Question 3.
```{r}
install.packages("readr")   # only once
library(readr)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
male_Aus <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/aus_athletics_male.csv')
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

rmarkdown::paged_table(male_Aus)
```

<br>


![](http://bcdanl.github.io/lec_figs/danl-310-hw2-q3.png)
<br>


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

male_Aus <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/aus_athletics_male.csv')

ggplot(male_Aus, aes(x = height, y = pcBfat)) +

  geom_point(
    aes(shape = sport, fill = sport, color = sport),
    size = 2,
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +

  scale_shape_manual(values = c(
    "basketball" = 21,  
    "field"      = 22,  
    "swimming"   = 23,  
    "track"      = 24, 
    "water polo" = 25   
  )) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "basketball" = "#C0392B",
    "field"      = "grey70",
    "swimming"   = "grey70",
    "track"      = "grey70",
    "water polo" = "grey70"
  )) +

  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "basketball" = "#C0392B",
    "field"      = "grey50",
    "swimming"   = "grey50",
    "track"      = "grey50",
    "water polo" = "grey50"
  )) +

  labs(
    x = "height (cm)",
    y = "% body fat",
    shape = "sport",
    fill = "sport",
    color = "sport"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
```{r}
# Track seems to have a lower percentage of body fat and smaller height to run faster. Basketball has a taller height and middle range body fat. 
```

## Question 4
Use the following data.frame for Question 4.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
titanic <- read_csv(
  'https://bcdanl.github.io/data/titanic_cleaned.csv')
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

rmarkdown::paged_table(titanic)
```

<br>


![](http://bcdanl.github.io/lec_figs/danl-310-hw2-q4.png)
<br>


```{r}
library(tidyverse)

titanic <- read_csv("https://bcdanl.github.io/data/titanic_cleaned.csv")

ggplot() +
  geom_density(
    data = titanic %>% select(age),  
    aes(x = age, y = after_stat(count), fill = "all passengers"),
    alpha = 0.9,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_density(
    data = filter(titanic, gender == "female"),
    aes(x = age, y = after_stat(count), fill = "females"),
    alpha = 1,
    color = NA
  ) +
  geom_density(
    data = filter(titanic, gender == "male"),
    aes(x = age, y = after_stat(count), fill = "males"),
    alpha = 1,
    color = NA
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ gender, ncol = 2) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "all passengers" = "grey80",
      "males" = "#0072B2",
      "females" = "#D55E00"
    ),
    breaks = c("all passengers", "males", "females"),
    name = NULL
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 25)) +

  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```
```{r}
# The average age of all passengers is between 20-40. More women survived then men on the titanic. 
```

![](http://bcdanl.github.io/lec_figs/danl-310-hw2-q5.png)

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggthemes)

ggplot(cows_filtered, aes(x = butterfat, fill = breed)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Ayrshire" = "#4daf4a",
      "Guernsey" = "#ff7f00",
      "Holstein-Friesian" = "#377eb8",
      "Jersey" = "#f781bf"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "butterfat contents",
    y = "density",
    fill = "breed"
  ) +
  theme_fivethirtyeight() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),

    axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 1, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, margin = margin(r = 10)),

    legend.title = element_text(size = 5, face = "bold"),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 5),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "lines"),
    legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "lines")
  )

```
```{r}
# The jersey cows have the highest butterfat contents of all of the cows. The holstein-friesian cows have the highest density. 
```

## Question 6

Provide both ggplot code and a simple comment to describe the yearly trend of GHG emissions for each sector.

```{r}
ghg_emissions %>%
  mutate(
    Sector = ifelse(
      Sector == "Industrial processes and product use",
      "Industrial processes",
      Sector
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, Sector) %>%
  summarise(total_emissions = sum(GHG_emissions, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = total_emissions, color = Sector)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "GHG emissions",
    color = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.6, "cm")
  )
```
```{r}
# Energy is the highest ghg emissions sector by far compared to the other. All the other sectors remain steady with their emissions. 
```

<br><br>

## Question 7

Provide both ggplot code and a simple comment to describe the yearly trend of United States of America's GHG emissions for each sector.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

ghg_emissions %>%
  filter(Party == "United States of America") %>%
  mutate(
    Sector = ifelse(
      Sector == "Industrial processes and product use",
      "Industrial processes",
      Sector
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, Sector) %>%
  summarise(total_emissions = sum(GHG_emissions, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = total_emissions, color = Sector)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "GHG emissions",
    color = "Sector"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),     
    legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm")         
  )
```
```{r}
# For just the US, the energy sector still remains the highest in ghg emissions. The lowest in the US is the LULUCF with the other remaing stedy. 
```

## Question 8

For each party, calculate the yearly percentage change in GHG emissions for each sector.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

ghg_percentchange_table <- ghg_emissions %>%
  mutate(
    Sector = ifelse(
      Sector == "Industrial processes and product use",
      "Industrial processes",
      Sector
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Party, Sector) %>%
  arrange(Year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_change = (GHG_emissions - lag(GHG_emissions)) /
                 lag(GHG_emissions) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Party, Sector, Year, GHG_emissions, pct_change) %>%
  arrange(Party, Sector, Year)

ghg_pct_table
```

<br><br>

## Question 9

Which party has reduced GHG emissions most from 1990 level to 2017 level in terms of the percentage change in GHG emissions?

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

ghg_reduce <- ghg_emissions %>%
  filter(Year %in% c(1990, 2017)) %>%
  group_by(Party, Year) %>%
  summarise(total_emissions = sum(GHG_emissions, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(Party, Year) %>%
  group_by(Party) %>%
  summarise(
    pct_change_1990_2017 =
      (total_emissions[Year == 2017] -
       total_emissions[Year == 1990]) /
       total_emissions[Year == 1990] * 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(pct_change_1990_2017)

ghg_reduce
```

<br><br>

```{r}

sector_reduce
```
